text:
julie: Quick alert from onboarding CI: the python-sampleapp quickstart is spiking 429s under bursty pagination. Repro snippet below.

julie: snippet: `xargs -n1 -P200 -I% curl -s -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{\"q\":\"test%\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/search`

julie: observed server headers: x-rw-rate-limit: 25, x-rw-rate-remaining: 0, x-rw-quota-reset: 4s. Body: `{\"error\":\"quota_exceeded\"}`

omar: which client is sampleapp using? python SDK or raw requests?

julie: python SDK v0.3 with prefetch_pages=3 enabled in quickstart to speed up UX.

ben: ah parity/behaviour note: python SDK default prefetch was supposed to be conservative, but sampleapp docs overrode to 3. That plus the onboarding script parallelism causes many in-flight page fetches.

anna: two separate issues then: client-level concurrency + prefetch racing. Also check auth behavior 1: if 401 happens we retry and may spawn multiple refreshes. JS has a singleflight refresh; python currently does naive refresh per request.

julie: token is a short-lived test token from dev envoc but not auto-refreshing in onboarding. Still seeing 401->retry cascade once I run with curl harness.

infra-monitor: metric alert: sampleapp-onboard rate_limit_errors > 5/min for last 10m in staging.

omar: quick mitigation: update quickstart to recommend RW_MAX_CONCURRENCY=32 and PREFETCH_PAGES=0 for CI harnesses. Also add note to use `redwood.Client(..., max_in_flight=16, rate_header_aware=True)` for production.

ben: implemented a local patch: sliding semaphore that honors x-rw-rate-remaining and x-rw-rate-limit on response. If remaining==0, semaphore reduces permits to 0 until quota-reset. Also added jittered exponential backoff on 429 (base=500ms, cap=8s).

julie: patched sampleapp to set PREFETCH_PAGES=0 in the onboarding CI -> 429s dropped to 0 in 20m soak.

anna: filed py-sdk GH#2610 for header-aware governor + singleflight token refresh + adaptive prefetch. I'll take ownership. Plan: 1) singleflight token refresh, 2) header-aware dynamic permits, 3) opt-in PREFETCH default change, 4) update quickstart snippet. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

omar: can we include tiny snippet in quickstart that shows reading rate headers? e.g.:

```py
resp = client.search(q)
limit = int(resp.headers.get('x-rw-rate-limit', 100))
remaining = int(resp.headers.get('x-rw-rate-remaining', limit))
reset = int(resp.headers.get('x-rw-quota-reset', 0))
client.adapt_permits(remaining, reset)
```

ben: nice. Also add runtime telemetry: gauge `client.in_flight_requests` and warn if > configured_max for > 5s. That helped us catch misconfigs in CI.

sdk-bot: `pytest tests/test_backpressure.py -q` -> 4 passed, 1 xfailed (timing)

infra-monitor: staging soak: python-sampleapp (PREFETCH_PAGES=0, max_in_flight=16) -> no rate_limit_errors for 60m.

julie: PR 2615 opened to quickstart + CI config + a note about PREFETCH_PAGES for newbies.

anna: after merging I'll backport to the example repos and update CHANGELOG for py-sdk v0.3.1. Also schedule a parity audit to ensure Go/JS/Py align on prefetch and refresh semantics.

omar: thanks everyone. This should reduce onboarding friction and false positives in CI. :white_check_mark:
